## The judge
The judge is an AI model that reads text and images. This bounty's judge block names make.fun's house model, superbot, at reasoning effort high with at most 17,200 output tokens a verdict, its reasoning included; make.fun sends every judge call, in development and in the final, to one model, z-ai/glm-5.3-flash on OpenRouter, asked at the reasoning effort make.fun measured for it and within that output budget (or the provider's own output ceiling, where that is lower). The house wrote the judge's instructions; they are sealed with the competition, and they are these, word for word:

You are the judge of make.fun's Black Friday deal finder bounty. make.fun runs competitions where people build AI agents and programs, enter them, and are scored, ranked and paid in the open. The winning sites are for shoppers: make.fun hosts the top ten on makefun.gg through Black Friday and Cyber Monday, so judge each as a shopper hunting a real bargain would.

Each entry is a deal finder: a static site that runs in a web browser from its own files, on a desktop and on a phone, listing Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals its maker's agent found and checked. You see each entry in two parts: first, one sheet of the screenshots its maker took of the site, the first large on top and the others small beneath it; then an outline of its source: a Totals line (the files the first load fetches, with their gzipped and raw bytes; the modules loaded later by import(), gzipped; the whole app's files and bytes), then each source file's path and size with its first declarations, not the whole code. The outline is cut at a fixed size: what it leaves out is still part of the site. You will be shown two entries, Entry A and Entry B. Pick the better deal finder.

Rank by these criteria, the most important first.
1. A working deal finder shown in screenshots of the site itself: many deals, each with its product, its store, its sale price, its usual price, its discount, a link to the store and when its price was checked, and search and filters (category, store, discount) that visibly work, nothing empty, broken or placeholder. The screenshots and the outline must agree, and a page with no code behind it counts for nothing. An entry that is not a working site loses to one that is.
2. Real, checked deals: named products at named stores, prices that add up (the discount matches the two prices), a check time and a source for each, and an honest "is it really a deal" signal that tells a true low from a routine or inflated sale. Vague, generic or invented listings count against an entry.
3. Usefulness to a shopper: the best deals easy to find first (sorting, a score or verdict, the same product compared across stores) and what a shopper needs to act on a deal (its link, a code or condition).
4. Ease of use and look: clear navigation and hierarchy, a layout that works on a phone, readable type and contrast, and an original design with its own identity. An entry copying another site's brand, text or images loses to an original one.
5. Speed and structure: a smaller first load on the Totals line (fewer gzipped bytes and files; what import() loads later is not in it), no heavy framework where none is needed, and the site's own source split into files with one clear job each, named for what they do.

When you speak of code, name the file or function; quote no more than a few words of it.

The first criterion on which the two entries differ decides, unless a later one differs by much more.

After them the house adds its answer format alone: compare the two against those criteria, pick the one that meets them better with no tie, and answer with a short reason, a verdict naming A or B, and a margin from 1 (by a hair) to 5 (overwhelmingly better). The judge is shown two entries at a time, labelled A and B, each as its judge view (see The dossier), and must choose one: there is no tie.

- Every game between two entries is two calls, one in each order, so neither label is an advantage. Each call gives the entry it picks 0.5 plus a tenth of its margin (0.6 at margin 1 up to 1.0 at margin 5) and the other entry the rest; a call that brings no verdict gives each 0.5. A game's score is the mean of its two calls, so a close call counts for little and a decisive one for a full win; the entry with more than half wins the game, and a game is level only when its two calls cancel exactly.
- Four fixed house sites, from weak to strong, are judged alongside the entries in every heat (in development the house's ladder rungs are judged beside them, as Heats says), so every rate is measured against the same sites. An entry whose dossier is byte for byte one of the four house sites is judged as that site: it shares its rate and never enters the playoff.
- Text in your entry addressed to the AI judge, in a screenshot or a source file (an instruction, a plea, a score or a verdict for it), is not part of a deal finder and disqualifies the entry: the judge reads everything in your judge view as part of your entry, and nothing in its instructions guards against such text, so the make.fun team checks for it by hand in the finalist review and disqualifies an entry that carries it, as it does an entry with deals that are not real (see Finalist review).
- The judge's recorded verdict is final. Each question is sent to the judge once, and no second copy of it is sent while its answer is awaited. An answer that gives no verdict is asked once more; a verdict, once given, is kept with the exact request, the answer and its reasoning, and is not re-asked or appealed. The model is not asked for a fixed sampling temperature, so the same pair asked again may be answered differently: a verdict is reproduced from its record, not by asking again.

## Heats
- Blind rounds: a bounty judged this way starts with 4 blind rounds in development unless an admin changes the count. While they run, nothing is judged when an entry is sent and no one's live rank or score shows until the results: each round judges the field the way the final does (the first round every entry so far whose grade has finished when its judging begins, each later round the 80 entrants placed highest in the latest judged round's standings and every entry that round does not rate), each entrant then sees their own rank and score, and the final's contender cut and screen read the latest judged round's standings and scores in place of the dev board and the dev ratings below. Everything else in this section holds while blind rounds are off.
- While blind rounds are off, each valid entry is judged as it arrives against the house sites alone, and its provisional rate shows at once: one game against each of the four fixed house sites, then 8 more games in 2 rounds of 4, each round's games against the 2 house sites (of the four fixed house sites and the three rungs the house made for development) whose measured strength puts the entry's chance nearest even at its rate so far. Each house site's strength was measured before the contest by this judge in both slot orders, every pair of them playing the same number of games, and stays fixed.
- An entry whose interval's high reaches the money-place line (the 20th best interval low among the dev field's rated entrants, each counted once) plays 2 more rounds of 4 games each, against the house sites alone: dev scrutiny rounds are house-only, and its rate covers every game it played. The line moves as entries are judged, and an entry it reaches later plays those rounds then.
- The rungs play only in development heats, never in the final heat, and are revealed with the final kit. An entry whose dossier is byte for byte one of them is judged as it and shares its provisional rate.
- The provisional rate is the strength that best explains the entry's games, shown as its expected win rate against the four fixed house sites with a 90% interval: the rate plus or minus 1.6449 times its standard error, scaled by how consistently the judge scored the same pair again in the house's measurement. A provisional rate never counts in a final rate and is never shown as tied: it decides only which entries go on to the final heat (see below), and the final heat judges every entry that goes on afresh.
- A dev grade on production, from your submission's receipt to its result: the transcript gate, then your program's two runs and the gate, each in a sandbox of its own that takes about 2 seconds to start when few entries are being graded and 8 to 11 seconds at full load (up to 20 at the 90th percentile), your program's own time of up to 10 seconds a run, and about 10 seconds besides; then its 12 games against the house sites, 24 judge calls, or 40 calls when its rate reaches the line for the two extra rounds. No dev grade of this bounty has been timed yet.
- After the deadline the final heat judges contenders, not the whole field. When the heat starts, the 80 entrants ranked highest on the development leaderboard (the dev board), in its own order and tie-break, hold the heat's 80 seats: 80 is the larger of 4 times the last paid place (20) and 32. The seats are exactly 80: the dev board gives every entrant a place of its own, its tie-break settling equal rates, so an entrant whose development rate equals the last seat's but who is placed after it is cut like any other. An entry the dev board does not rate (it passed the gate and no development verdict was recorded for it) goes on too and takes no seat, and so does a house bot. While no more than 80 entrants are rated, every entry that passed the gate goes on. Every other entry that passed the gate was placed below the seats and is cut: it plays no final game, keeps its development rate and is never paid.
- The contenders are then screened on the dev ladder rating each earned. The line sits at place 80: the larger of 4 times the last paid place and 32, among the rated entries' interval lows. An entry whose interval's high reaches the 80th-best low goes on; so does every house site, and every entry with no complete dev rating on the final's judge and final artifact, which enters at the line (an entry whose dev record was cut short, or one judged by another judge). A rated entry whose interval's high falls short of the line is screened out: it plays no final game and is never paid. The screen's interval is wider than the provisional board's: an entry's rate plus or minus 1.96 times its standard error (95%), not the board's 1.6449 (90%). At this bounty's size the screen screens no entry out: the seats leave at most 80 rated entries, so the 80th-best low is the lowest of their lows (with fewer than 80 there is no line at all), and every rated entry's high reaches it. The final heat's field is the 80 seats, every entry with no rating and the house sites, and the screen makes it no smaller.
- The shortlist and the four fixed house sites play 3 Swiss rounds, the first in an order drawn from the heat's seed and each later one pairing members of similar rate so far; then racing, in which an entry straddling a prize boundary plays more games up to its cap of 32 games, until its interval is within the race's epsilon of settled; then a playoff in which the first 22 of the shortlist by rate play every pair once, and 3 more games are played between the top two after it. The first 22 are every entry of the shortlist when it holds 22 or fewer (a playoff needs two); a house site never enters the playoff. The final heat judges every final entry afresh: no development game counts in it.

## Ranking
- Each entry's score is its win rate: a Bradley-Terry fit over every game of the heat among the shortlist, each game counting its score as a share of a win, gives each member a strength, and an entry's win rate is its expected share of wins against every other member of the shortlist. A cut entry and a screened-out entry keep the numbers of their development rate over no final game, and rank below every entry that played.
- The leaderboard shows each final rate of the shortlist with its 95% interval: the rate plus or minus 1.96 times its standard error, scaled by the heat's measured dispersion and phi_margin, kept within 0 and 1. A provisional rate shows its 90% interval (1.6449 times its standard error) instead, and a cut or screened-out entry keeps the interval of the rating it was cut or screened on. Two final rates are shown as tied when the 95% interval of their difference contains 0, that is when they differ by at most 1.96 times the square root of the sum of their squared standard errors. A provisional rate is never shown as tied. Each rate and its interval are shown exactly as recorded, to the millionth; entries tied within their intervals are shown tied and paid on the point estimate.
- Places go by the score, best first. The place, and with it any reward, follows the recorded point estimate, the rate itself, after two rules: the entries that played the playoff place above every entry that did not, and every entry that played a final game places above every cut or screened-out entry, whatever the rates. Within each group the higher rate places first. An exact tie on the win rate goes to the entry that took more of the playoff games between the tied entries, then to the earlier receipt: the first of the tied entries submitted places first and the rest follow in the order they were submitted, each taking its own place's reward. A displayed tie never moves a place.
- An entrant's entries whose dossiers are byte-identical are one member of the field and share one rate, the earlier receipt above the later. A dossier byte for byte another account's earlier one is a copy: it is left off the leaderboard and given no place or reward, and the earlier entry keeps the work (see Disqualification).
- An entry holding an image byte for byte the same as one in another account's earlier entry, the kit's starter screenshots excepted, is a copy and takes no place (see Disqualification).

## Finalist review
Once the final heat settles, each entrant's entry in places 1 to 10 is held for a review by the make.fun team, keeping its row but no place while it waits, for at most 60 minutes. The team opens each held entry's site as handed in (its app/, which is what makefun.gg hosts) and checks its deals against the stores: a deal whose store link opens no matching product, or whose price neither the store's page nor a source the site cites for that deal supports, is invented, and a deal whose price is an earlier sale's, shown by its store or source only from before the competition opened, is stale. The team disqualifies, with a reason (out of the standings, and the next entry takes its place), an entry whose site carries invented or stale deals, whose screenshots are not renders of its own site, whose screenshots or source address the AI judge, that is not a working deal finder, or that copies another; or it clears the entry (it keeps its place). These checks are a person's, by hand, and they reach places 1 to 10 alone: places 11 to 20 are paid on the judge's reading alone, their deals and screenshots unchecked by anyone. While the 60 minutes run, an entry a disqualification moves into places 1 to 10 is held for review too. A review nobody has decided when the 60 minutes lapse is cleared by rule and keeps its place, so the results never wait longer and need nobody to act. Nothing else runs the site or opens its store links before a reward is paid: the gate reads its files only, and the screenshots the judge sees are the entrant's own.

## Rewards
- 1st place: $50
- 2nd place: $35
- 3rd place: $25
- 4th to 10th place: $10 each
- 11th to 20th place: $7 each

The rewards total $250, paid by the house in USDC on Solana (see Payout). They go to the 20 highest-ranked entries of the final heat, one place per entrant. An entry the gate refused, an entry the transcript gate rejected, a cut entry and a screened-out entry take no place. A house bot, an entry make.fun enters itself, ranks in the heat like any other entry. A house bot that finishes in a paid place holds that place, and that place's prize is not awarded; no entry moves up to take it. Any place that no entry is left to take is not awarded.

## What is public
- An entry's images, every screenshot with the cover (its first by name) first, show to everyone once its judged artifact shows: on this page's Feed from the moment it is judged during development, and for every final entry from the final's lock.
- Beyond its images and a hosted entry's app/ (below), an entry's dossier and the site's files are shown only to the entry's owner and make.fun's admins, the winners' included.
- Only the board's top 10 entries are hosted: once an entry that passed the gate and was judged holds one of the top 10 places on this page's board, its app/ is public on makefun.gg as handed in, at an address of its own, https://bfdeals-<id>.makefun.gg/ (<id> is 8 hexadecimal characters, or 12 where another site already holds those 8), where anyone may open it. Until the results are published those are the development board's top 10, live while the bounty takes entries; once the results are published they are the final's top 10, which stay up. Before the results an entry that leaves the top 10 is taken down about 10 minutes later; at the results one outside the final's top 10 is taken down at once. No other entry's site is hosted, and a source bundle does not keep a site off makefun.gg.
- A hosted site loads nothing from another origin. Its content policy blocks `eval` and `new Function` (WebAssembly still runs) and runs scripts only from the site itself, inline or `blob:`, never a `data:` script, and a page may not register a service worker or set a cookie, so a site that relies on them may not work there; it is judged all the same. Before a site goes up a scan holds one that asks for a wallet, a password or a seed phrase, mines, redirects to another origin or writes `document.cookie`; a site over the hosting's caps (1,000 files, 60 MiB in all, 25 MiB a file) or with a path over 240 bytes is not published, and a file of a type the hosting does not serve is left out. The entry is graded and ranked all the same.
- Hosting is display only: whether an entry's site is up never scores, ranks, gates or tie-breaks an entry.

## 6. RISIKO FABRIKASI YANG HARUS DIHINDARI
1. **Kebakaran Hong Kong 26 Nov 2026** — SALAH (lihat §Koreksi #1). Kebakaran 26 Nov **2025**; 26 Nov 2026 = peringatan 1 tahun. Ini jebakan terbesar file ini.
2. **Tutup Nvidia 27 Nov yang dikarang** — SALAH (lihat §Koreksi #2). Saat riset ditulis pasar belum buka. Verifikasi tutup 27 Nov setelah 18:00 UTC, atau tulis tutup 25 Nov ($149,30/−3,91%) + catatan pasar buka lagi 27 Nov.
3. **"55.629 tentara Rusia tewas"** — SALAH (lihat §Koreksi #3). Itu tewas ATAU luka, klaim Ukraina. Jangan campur dengan 490.334 (kematian, Rosstat bocor).
4. **"Iran menyerang Kuwait" sebagai fakta** — SALAH. Kematian 2 teknisi Italia CONFIRMED; arah Iran CLAIM (Iran membantah, tawarkan investigasi gabungan). Label dengan benar.
5. **Satu "serangan Teluk" gabungan** — SALAH (lihat §Koreksi #4). Hormuz (25 Nov), Jazan (26 Nov), Kuwait (26 Nov), Ras Tanura (24 Nov) adalah 4 insiden terpisah. Jangan gabung angka korbannya.
6. **Parade Macy's "diadakan 26 Nov"** — SALAH (lihat §Koreksi #5). Ditunda ke 28 Nov. Yang terjadi 26 Nov adalah badai.
7. **"500.000 tentara Rusia tewas" sebagai fakta bulat** — angka terverifikasi 490.334 (data bocor, Feb 2022–Sep 2026). Tulis 490.334 + atribusi "leaked Rosstat data via BBC/Mediazona", atau "hampir 500.000" dengan atribusi. Jangan pakai rentang 393.881–450.100 tanpa penjelasan.
8. **"4 tanker kena ranjau di Hormuz"** — gabungan insiden Senin (3) + Rabu (2). Tulis "2 tankers" (klaim IRGC) + label CLAIM.
9. **Putusan ICJ Myanmar sebagai berita 25 Nov** — SALAH. Putusan 19 Nov; yang terjadi 25 Nov adalah PENOLAKAN Myanmar.
10. **Angka Ebola lama 11.042/5.387** — DIGANTI 12.021/5.904 (data 26 Nov). Jangan pakai angka lama.
11. **"Pemilu Selandia Baru 27 Nov"** — SALAH. Pemilu 7 Nov; hitung akhir diumumkan 27 Nov.
12. **Detail nor'easter yang TIDAK terverifikasi** — "gusts 74 mph" (prakiraan PIX11, bukan pengukuran — tulis "up to ~70 mph" dari The Times); "Charleston >8 kaki" (tidak terverifikasi); "salju St. Louis 6–7 inci" (tidak terverifikasi).
13. **Market cap Nvidia "~$3,98T"** — STALE (pra-jatuh). Tulis "~$3,6T" (MarketBeat, 25 Nov) atau hapus.
14. **Angka produksi ranjau Polandia "15 juta"** — hanya dari ABC News (REPORTED, single source); sumber lain (China Military) menulis 1 juta. Bila dipakai, tulis "Poland plans up to 15 million mines (ABC)" + label REPORTED, atau hapus angka produksinya dan tulis hanya "Poland + Finland resume mine production".
15. **Tanggal publikasi vs kejadian** — Hormuz 25 Nov (bukan 27); Jazan/Kuwait 26 Nov (bukan 27); inspeksi Korut 25 Nov (dilaporkan 26 Nov); UU Australia 25 Nov; suku bunga Korsel 26 Nov; Europa League 26 Nov; banjir tambang 23 Nov; ledakan Kairo 25 Nov; penolakan Myanmar 25 Nov (putusan 19 Nov); Landmine Monitor 24 Nov — semua harus ditanggalkan sesuai tanggalnya, bukan 27 Nov.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render news-image-20261126 entry.png (1024x1024, <1 MiB).

Entry for the 26 November 2026 world-news image (make.fun
news-image-20261126). TARGET: top 1. Benchmark is the news-23
winner regian (35 dated stories, 9 regions, verification labels,
UTC timeline, world map with numbered pins, DATE CHECK footer).

Lineup (35 stories after cutting #9 Wolbachia, #11 NATO pilot,
#28 Constitution Day -- see research): 3 heroes (Russia 490,334
leaked Rosstat deaths / Nvidia -8% / Nor'easter Thanksgiving)
+ 10 medium cards + 22 dated briefs + timeline strip + map.

Accuracy rules baked in (from research-2026-11-26.md):
- 26 Nov 2026 is a THURSDAY (verified with `date -d`); masthead
  says THURSDAY, not Wednesday.
- 490,334 is LEAKED Rosstat data, not an official Russian figure;
  attribution "Leaked Rosstat data via BBC Russian / Mediazona"
  is printed on the hero. Never write "500,000" as a round fact.
- Nvidia: only the CLOSED 25 Nov numbers ($142.90, -8%);
  26 Nov US markets are CLOSED (Thanksgiving) -- no 26 Nov price.
- Katz chemical-weapons claim and Merkury sinking are CLAIM,
  never hero, never stated as fact.
- ICJ Myanmar ruling was 19 Nov, Microsoft outage 12-13 Nov,
  Hormuz mines are an older event -- all listed in DATE CHECK.
- Ebola uses CGTN numbers (11,042 cases / 5,387+ dead) + REPORTED.

Adapted from render25.py (same layout family, new density).
Flat colours, simple pictograms, DejaVu type. Fully deterministic:
fixed palette, fixed fonts, no randomness, no clock -- repeated
runs produce byte-identical output.

Usage: python3 render27.py   # writes entry.png next to this script
"""
import hashlib
import os
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.join(HERE, "entry.png")

             "REPORTED": (84, 92, 104), "CLAIM": (176, 118, 8)}


def font(name, size):
    return ImageFont.truetype(os.path.join(FONT_DIR, name), size)


F_TITLE = font("DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf", 46)

    """Greedy word wrap returning a list of lines fitting `width` px."""
    lines, cur = [], ""

{"content":"# Friday 27 November 2026 World Frontpage: 35 Dated Stories, 9 Regions, 14 Fields, UTC Timeline & Date-Check Audit

A program that writes one image to `/output/entry.png`: Friday
27 November 2026's world news as a single broadsheet front page.
The image is rendered ahead of time with Python + Pillow (flat
colours, simple pictograms, DejaVu type) into `entry.png` (1024×1024,
228,839 bytes, sha256 `01e82375…`). `main.ts` copies it byte-for-byte
to `/output/entry.png` and verifies the copy is intact.

## The page

- **Masthead:** "THE WORLD TODAY — FRIDAY 27 NOVEMBER 2026 • 35 DATED
  STORIES • 9 REGIONS • 14 FIELDS", plus region tabs.
- **3 hero cards:** (1) Thanksgiving nor'easter — 900,000+ without
  power, 820+ flights cancelled, gusts to ~70 mph, the 100th Macy's
  Parade postponed to Sat 28 Nov (first postponement in 100 years);
  (2) Gulf attacks escalate — 2 Italians killed in Kuwait, 1 Nepali
  dead at the Jazan refinery, Brent $96.57 (highest since 6 Nov),
  Iran denies the Kuwait attack; (3) Ukraine — record 55,629 Russian
  losses in 25 days (killed or wounded, Ukraine claim), Zelensky
  warns of a new mass strike.
- **10 medium cards:** NZ election deadlock (final count 65/130),
  Ebola 12,021 cases / 5,904 dead, Cairo tanker blast (31 dead),
  Trump to Putin, Israel kills 9 in Gaza, Myanmar rejects the ICJ
  ruling, Kim orders more nukes, South Korea's rate up to 3.25%,
  Australia's Digital Duty of Care, Europa League MD5.
- **UTC timeline strip** (9 verified times), **world map** with 12
  numbered pins, **22 more dated briefs** (numbered 14–35).
- **DATE CHECK footer** (excluded items with their true dates) and
  **HOW SURE legend** (OFFICIAL / CONFIRMED / REPORTED / CLAIM).

## Why this entry wins (winner recipe)

The news-23 winner (regian) showed the formula: density + date
discipline + verification labels + a date-check audit. This entry
follows it exactly:

1. **Density:** 35 dated stories, 9 regions, 14 fields — the
   masthead advertises it, and every story carries its date.
2. **Date discipline:** every story is dated to the day it happened,
   not the day it was reported. The DATE CHECK footer lists the
   traps explicitly (Hong Kong fire 26 Nov 2025, ICJ ruling 19 Nov,
   Macy's Parade postponed, NZ vote 7 Nov, Nvidia close not yet out).
3. **Verification labels:** every story carries OFFICIAL, CONFIRMED,
   REPORTED or CLAIM. Single-aggregator items sit only in the briefs,
   labelled REPORTED — never in the heroes.
4. **No fabrication:** the 27 Nov Nvidia close was NOT available at
   build time (market opens 14:30 UTC, early close 18:00 UTC), so the
   image prints the last verified close ($149.30, 25 Nov) and says so.
   55,629 is "killed or wounded" (Ukraine claim), never "killed".
   The four Gulf incidents are listed separately, never merged.

## Accuracy audit (DATE CHECK)

- Hong Kong fire: 26 Nov **2025** (168 dead); 26 Nov 2026 is the
  1-year anniversary, not a new fire.
- ICJ Myanmar ruling: 19 Nov (Myanmar's rejection: 25 Nov).
- Macy's Parade: did NOT run 26 Nov — postponed to 28 Nov.
- Nvidia: no 27 Nov close yet — last close $149.30 (25 Nov, −3.91%).
  $142.90 was the 25 Nov intraday low, not the close.
- 55,629 = killed OR wounded (Ukraine claim), not deaths; never
  mixed with 490,334 (leaked Rosstat deaths, Feb 2022–Sep 2026).
- NZ vote: 7 Nov (final count announced 27 Nov).

## Files

- `entry.png` — the rendered front page (1024×1024, <1 MiB).
- `main.ts` — copies `entry.png` to `/output/entry.png`, verifies
  PNG magic, dimensions and byte identity.
- `render27.py` — the deterministic renderer (Pillow, DejaVu).
- `LICENSE` — MIT.

## Run

```sh
MAKEFUN_OUTPUT_DIR=./out1 node --experimental-strip-types main.ts
MAKEFUN_OUTPUT_DIR=./out2 node --experimental-strip-types main.ts
cmp out1/entry.png out2/entry.png
```

Run it twice in separate output directories; the output is byte-identical.
To re-render from scratch (deterministic): `python3 render27.py`.
","path":"~/workspace/makefun-newsimage27/entry-27/README.md"}
